question.prompt: What is the greatest possible sum of the digits in the base-seven representation of a positive integer less than \(2019?\)

solutions.title: Bound the base-seven digits
solutions.explanation:
The size restriction limits the leading base-seven digit, while every digit is at most \(6\). First convert the largest allowed integer, \(2018\), by repeated division:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2018&=7\cdot288+2,\\
288&=7\cdot41+1,\\
41&=7\cdot5+6,\\
5&=7\cdot0+5.
\end{aligned}
\]
Reading the remainders upward gives \(2018=(5612)_7\).

Write every allowed number with four digits, using leading zeros when necessary. Its first digit is at most \(5\).

If the first digit is at most \(4\), the digit sum is at most
\[
4+6+6+6=22.
\]
If the first digit is \(5\), the other three digits cannot all be \(6\), since \((5666)_7>(5612)_7\). At least one is therefore at most \(5\), giving a digit sum at most
\[
5+5+6+6=22.
\]
Finally, \((4666)_7<(5612)_7=2018\), and its digits sum to \(22\). Thus the bound is attained, and the greatest possible sum is \(\boxed{22}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
